Guha
------------------------------------------
Guha of the Rāmāyaṇa is a glorious example to show that great men like राम paid greater attention to the character of persons and honoured them than their birth and caste. शबरी is another such character met with in the same epic.
Guha was the chieftain of the forest tribes living at Śṛṅgaverapura. He was a great friend of दशरथ, राम’s ड़थेर्. After banishment when राम reached the forest गुह was his host who entertained him with love and affection. He also helped राम, along with सीता and लक्ष्मण, to cross the गङ्गा and reach its southern bank.
When राम was staying at the चित्रकूट mountain, भरत arrived at the forest, with his army, to take him back. Suspecting that he must have come to harm राम, गुह prepared his men to face भरत and fight him if necessary. However, after learning of his real motive, गुह regretted his hasty action, entertained भरत and his party and then helped them to cross the river गङ्गा.
Guha is also one of the names of सुब्रह्मण्य, known by other names too such as स्कन्द, Śaravaṇabhava, कुमार, and षण्मुख. He is the son of शिव and पार्वती and the commander-in-chief of the army of the gods. See SUBRAHMAṆYA for details.
